question: Which functional group is polar, containing an unsymmetrical distribution of charge between oxygen and hydrogen atoms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alcohols**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Alcohols** contain the hydroxyl (-OH) group, which is highly **polar** due to the significant difference in electronegativity between oxygen and hydrogen atoms.
 
• The oxygen atom in the -OH group attracts the shared electron pair more strongly, creating a **partial negative charge** on oxygen and a **partial positive charge** on hydrogen.
 
• The presence of this asymmetrical charge distribution makes alcohols capable of forming **hydrogen bonds**, contributing to their solubility in water.
 
• Alcohols are commonly found in various chemical processes and are widely used in industries for **solvent applications, fuel additives, and chemical synthesis**.
